correctness.rationale: Exact Cayley-rooted-forest counting gives P(C_n=m)=m(n)_m/n^(m+1), and conditional restriction to cyclic vertices is a uniform permutation; fixed-point indicators give the exact Bin(n,1/n) marginal. Therefore conditional E(F_n|C_n)=1, exact covariance zero, and positive KL information for n>=2. The finite KL decomposition with Poisson(1) as reference is exact; a rencontres chi-square bound D(Q_m||P)<=(e*2^(m+1)+1)/(m+1)! and dominated convergence yield the candidate constant, while a uniform likelihood expansion establishes D(Bin(n,1/n)||P)=O(n^-2). A standard-library standalone checker passed 341 assertions including exhaustive enumeration of all maps through n=6, finite distribution identities, exact factorial moments, and entropy-chain comparisons. The numerical constant was computed from 30 terms with certified tail <1.5e-24; this does not replace the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact conditional permutation law and classical random mapping enumerations are acknowledged prior work. A close full-text primary comparison (Hansen–Jaworski 2010, all 19 pages examined) covers conditional component sizes and Poisson–Dirichlet limits but not this fixed-point/cyclic-core mutual-information asymptotic. Soria 1996 treats marginal random-mapping limit laws rather than the sharp information constant. Actual published-finding corpus and own-ledger claim searches found related but non-dominating statements. The new quantitative n^-1 entropy deficit, including its nonzero exact coefficient despite identically zero covariance, has not been identified in the inspected material. Unavailable archival Flajolet–Odlyzko full text and implicit consequences of general combinatorial probability methods remain explicit risks.
residual_risks: Flajolet–Odlyzko (1990) complete archival manuscript was not accessible for full-text inspection. Only bibliographic and abstract scope were checked; the source was not represented as non-covering.
The exact conditional mapping/permutation law is classical and general; an unlocated information-theoretic application or general entropy theorem could contain or imply the same coefficient.
Search and inspected-literature coverage is bounded and does not establish absolute historical priority.

value.rationale: Both counts are natural intrinsic statistics of a uniform functional graph. Their exact covariance vanishes, but dependence remains and has a nonzero universal information coefficient of order n^-1. The precise constant is determined by rare small cyclic cores, while the typical cyclic core is of order sqrt(n); this identifies a mathematically meaningful hidden-dependence mechanism not visible in first and second moments. It supplies an exact and reproducible invariant useful for comparing information carried by coarse descriptions of random mappings. No grander downstream theorem is assumed.
